batch: 7 (chs 34-45, the narrative of the fall - scenes)

units.characteristics: the reneged repentance; the good act undone; liberty withheld recoiling
units.gist: GEM - the covenant to FREE the Hebrew slaves, then reneged: 'you recently REPENTED and did what was right... but then you TURNED AROUND and profaned my name when each took back his slaves'; 'you have not obeyed me by proclaiming LIBERTY; behold, I proclaim to you LIBERTY to the sword, pestilence, and famine' - repentance done and then undone; liberty denied to others recoiling as liberty-to-death

units.characteristics: consistent multi-generational obedience as a rebuke to disobedience toward God
units.gist: GEM - the Rechabites who for generations KEPT their forefather Jonadab's command (no wine, tents, no vineyards); God holds them up: 'the sons of Jonadab have KEPT the command their father gave them... but THIS PEOPLE HAS NOT OBEYED ME'; human faithfulness to a mere ancestor's word shaming the nation's disobedience to the living God

units.characteristics: the word burned yet indestructible; the fearless (shameless) rejection vs the trembling hearers
units.gist: GEM - the scroll dictated and read; the officials 'turned to one another IN FEAR'; but king Jehoiakim cuts it column by column and burns it, 'yet NEITHER THE KING NOR HIS SERVANTS WAS AFRAID, nor did they tear their garments'; the LORD hid Baruch and Jeremiah; then 'take ANOTHER scroll... and many similar words were added' - the word rejected but indestructible; the unmoved heart vs the trembling one

units.characteristics: the prophet in the pit; the outsider's compassion; the fearful king who knows but will not act
units.gist: GEM - Jeremiah beaten, imprisoned, thrown into the MUDDY CISTERN to die; EBED-MELECH the Ethiopian eunuch (an outsider) courageously appeals to the king and gently rescues him (the old rags to cushion the ropes); Zedekiah's secret, waffling consultations - 'I am AFRAID of the Judeans', knowing the truth ('obey and it shall be well with you') but unable to act on it - suffering faithfulness, an outsider's kindness, a vacillating fearful king

units.characteristics: the fall; the rescuer rescued because he trusted
units.gist: GEM - the fall of Jerusalem (Zedekiah's sons slain before his blinded eyes); then the word to Ebed-melech: 'I will surely SAVE YOU, and you shall not fall by the sword... BECAUSE YOU HAVE PUT YOUR TRUST IN ME, declares the LORD' - the outsider who rescued the prophet is himself delivered, and the ground named as his TRUST

units.characteristics: generous trust that refuses to suspect evil, and its tragic cost
units.gist: Gedaliah the good governor; warned of Ishmael's plot to kill him, 'GEDALIAH WOULD NOT BELIEVE them'; 'you are speaking falsely of Ishmael'; and Ishmael murders him at a shared meal - a noble, generous trust that refused to believe evil of another, and the tragedy when that trust is betrayed (charity toward a man not always safe, yet not condemned)

units.characteristics: asking guidance one has already decided to ignore; the vow to obey broken when the answer displeases
units.gist: GEM - the remnant asks Jeremiah to pray, vowing 'whether it is GOOD OR BAD, WE WILL OBEY the voice of the LORD'; God says STAY, do not go to Egypt, 'do not fear... I am with you'; but they call it a lie - 'YOU ARE TELLING A LIE' - and go to Egypt anyway; seeking divine guidance while already resolved to do one's own will

units.characteristics: the defiant heart that inverts cause and effect; open rebellion
units.gist: GEM - in Egypt the people openly refuse: 'as for the word you have spoken... WE WILL NOT LISTEN to you. But we will do everything we have VOWED, to make offerings to the QUEEN OF HEAVEN... since we left off offering to her WE HAVE LACKED EVERYTHING' - the fully inverted heart crediting the idol for past prosperity and blaming God-worship for its troubles; hardened, defiant rebellion

units.characteristics: the discouraged self-pity; seek not great things for yourself; life itself as the gift
units.gist: GEM - the word to Baruch: 'you said, WOE IS ME! the LORD has added SORROW to my pain; I am WEARY with my groaning, and I FIND NO REST'; God's answer - 'do you SEEK GREAT THINGS FOR YOURSELF? SEEK THEM NOT, for I am bringing disaster on all flesh; BUT I WILL GIVE YOU YOUR LIFE as a prize of war' - discouragement met with a re-scaling of desire and the gift of life itself
